core_obligations: Dispose of one direction with the base change statement for flat modules and assume for the converse that the tensor product of M with the second piece and the localization of M at f are both flat (proof lines 25715-25719).

Introduce the glueable replacement of M and show that if that replacement is flat then the kernel of the comparison map M to it has vanishing tensor product with the direct sum of the two pieces, so the kernel is zero by the faithfulness statement and M may be replaced by its glueable replacement (proof lines 25720-25727).

Take an arbitrary module N and reduce flatness of M to the vanishing of the first Tor group of M with N, then use the short exact sequence of the glueing pair to see that f is a nonzerodivisor on the first Tor group of the second piece with N and invertible on the higher ones (proof lines 25728-25744).

Transfer those divisibility properties to the first and second Tor groups of the tensor product of M with the second piece, using the flatness of that tensor product, the spectral sequence of the change of rings example and the description of flat modules as filtered colimits of finite free modules (proof lines 25745-25755).

Write the exact sequence coming from the glueing property of M, display the relevant part of its long exact sequence of Tor groups in a diagram, and conclude that the first Tor group of M with N vanishes, which is the flatness of M (proof lines 25756-25770).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case where M is glueable, using the glueable replacement and the faithfulness statement (proof lines 25715-25727).
Reduce flatness to the vanishing of a first Tor group against an arbitrary module N (proof lines 25728-25730).
Extract from the exact sequence of the glueing pair that f is a nonzerodivisor on the first Tor group of the second piece and invertible on the higher ones (proof lines 25733-25744).
Transfer this to the tensor product using flatness, a spectral sequence and Lazard's theorem, then read the conclusion off the displayed diagram (proof lines 25745-25770).
difficulty_reason: The statement shows that flatness of a module for a glueing pair is detected on the two pieces even when the module is not glueable: it is flat over the base exactly when its tensor product with the second piece is flat over that piece and its localization at the element is flat over the localization (statement lines 25707-25713). The proof first reduces to the glueable replacement, then reformulates flatness as the vanishing of the first Tor group against an arbitrary test module, and the hard part is a two-step computation: the exact sequence of the glueing pair shows that the element acts as a nonzerodivisor on the first Tor group of the second piece and invertibly on the higher ones, and those properties are transferred to the tensor product of M with that piece by using the flatness hypothesis together with a spectral sequence and the description of flat modules as filtered colimits of finite free modules (proof lines 25715-25770). The conclusion then follows from the displayed exact sequence.
